notes.summary: Economy gives about 2 to 3 questions per paper. Past papers ask most about government schemes (name, year, aim), Five-Year Plans, budget and tax terms, RBI tools, national income terms and basic micro concepts. Learn definitions word for word: options often differ by one word, such as 'excluding borrowings'.

concepts.title: Basic concepts
concepts.body:
• Adam Smith is the father of economics (The Wealth of Nations, 1776). J.M. Keynes is the father of macroeconomics (General Theory, 1936).
  • Microeconomics studies one consumer, firm or market; macroeconomics studies the whole economy (national income, inflation, employment).
  • Law of demand: price up, demand down (other things equal). Exceptions: Giffen goods, Veblen (status) goods.
  • Goods: normal (demand rises with income), inferior (demand falls with income), substitutes (tea and coffee), complements (car and petrol).
  • Budget line: all combinations of two goods a consumer can buy with a given income and prices. Indifference curve: combinations giving equal satisfaction. Isoquant: input combinations giving the same output.
  • Production possibility curve: maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with given resources. Opportunity cost: value of the next best option given up.
  • Costs: fixed (rent), variable (raw material), marginal (cost of one more unit).
Market formMeaning
Perfect competitionMany sellers, identical product, price taker
MonopolyOne seller, no close substitute
DuopolyTwo sellers
OligopolyFew big sellers
Monopolistic competitionMany sellers, differentiated products (brands)
MonopsonyOne buyer

Sectors: primary (agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry), secondary (manufacturing, construction, electricity), tertiary (services: trade, transport, banking). India is a mixed economy.

Laws: Gresham's law (bad money drives out good money); Say's law (supply creates its own demand); Engel's law (as income rises, the share spent on food falls).

concepts.title: National income
concepts.body:
TermMeaning
GDPValue of all final goods and services produced inside the country in a year
GNPGDP + net factor income from abroad
NNPGNP − depreciation
National incomeNNP at factor cost
Factor costMarket price − indirect taxes + subsidies
Personal incomeIncome received by people from all sources before personal income tax
Disposable incomePersonal income − direct taxes
Per capita incomeNational income ÷ population
  • Three methods: product (value added), income, and expenditure.
  • The National Statistics Office (NSO), under MoSPI, estimates national income. CSO (1951) and NSSO (1950) were merged into NSO in 2019.
  • Dadabhai Naoroji made the first estimate of India's national income (1867 to 1868). The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis.
  • The International Comparison Programme compares price levels and computes purchasing power parities (PPP) so GDP can be compared across countries.

concepts.title: Inflation and price indices
concepts.body:
• Inflation: a sustained rise in the general price level. Demand-pull (too much demand) and cost-push (costlier inputs).
  • Deflation: falling prices. Disinflation: inflation slowing down. Stagflation: high inflation with low growth and high unemployment. Hyperinflation: very fast price rise.
  • Headline inflation counts all items; core inflation leaves out food and fuel.
IndexReleased by
Wholesale Price Index (WPI)Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce)
Consumer Price Index (CPI) rural, urban, combinedNSO, MoSPI
CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW)Labour Bureau
Index of Industrial Production (IIP)NSO, MoSPI

Since 2016, the RBI follows flexible inflation targeting: CPI inflation of 4%, with a band of 2% to 6%.

concepts.title: RBI and monetary policy
concepts.body:
• RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934 (Hilton Young Commission). Nationalised on 1 January 1949. Headquarters: Mumbai (first in Kolkata). First Governor: Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor: C.D. Deshmukh.
  • Functions: issues currency (the Re 1 note and coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance), banker to the government, banker's bank, lender of last resort, keeper of foreign exchange reserves.
  • Monetary Policy Committee (2016): 6 members, chaired by the RBI Governor, who has a casting vote. It sets the repo rate.
ToolMeaning
Repo rateRate at which RBI lends short-term to banks against securities
Reverse repo / Standing Deposit FacilityRate RBI pays banks for parking money with it
Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)Emergency overnight borrowing by banks, above repo
Bank rateLong-term lending rate of RBI, without securities
CRRShare of deposits banks must keep with RBI as cash
SLRShare of deposits banks must keep themselves in cash, gold or government securities
Open Market OperationsRBI buying or selling government securities

To fight inflation, the RBI raises repo, CRR or SLR (less money in the system). Qualitative tools: margin requirements, credit rationing, moral suasion.

concepts.title: Banks and banking laws
concepts.body:
• Nationalisation: 14 banks on 19 July 1969 (deposits over Rs 50 crore); 6 more in 1980.
  • State Bank of India: formed in 1955 from the Imperial Bank of India (1921).
  • Punjab National Bank (1894) is often called the first bank fully run by Indians.
  • Regional Rural Banks: 1975. Lead Bank Scheme: 1969.
  • Payments banks (Nachiket Mor committee) accept deposits but cannot lend. Small finance banks lend to small units.
  • Development banks: NABARD (1982, agriculture, Mumbai), EXIM Bank (1982), NHB (1988, housing), SIDBI (1990, small industry, Lucknow).
  • DICGC insures each depositor up to Rs 5 lakh per bank (since 2020).
  • Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016: resolution within 180 days, extendable by 90 days.
  • UPI was launched in 2016 by NPCI. M1 is narrow money; M3 is broad money.
  • Narasimham Committee (1991) suggested banking reforms.

concepts.title: Budget, deficits and taxes
concepts.body:
• The budget is the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112). First budget of independent India: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty, 26 November 1947. Since 2017 it is presented on 1 February and the railway budget is merged into it.
  • Revenue receipts: taxes and non-tax income (dividends, fees). Capital receipts: borrowings, disinvestment, loan recoveries.
  • Revenue expenditure creates no asset (salaries, interest, subsidies, pensions). Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities (roads, buildings, machinery, loans given).
DeficitFormula
Fiscal deficitTotal expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings
Revenue deficitRevenue expenditure − revenue receipts
Primary deficitFiscal deficit − interest payments
  • FRBM Act: 2003. Finance Commission (Article 280) shares taxes with states.
  • Direct taxes (paid by the person taxed): income tax, corporation tax. Indirect taxes (passed on to the buyer): GST, customs duty, excise on petroleum and liquor.
  • GST started on 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment). The GST Council (Article 279A) is chaired by the Union Finance Minister. CGST and SGST on sales within a state; IGST on sales between states. From 22 September 2025 most goods moved to two main rates, 5% and 18%.
  • Progressive tax: rate rises with income. Regressive: falls as income rises. Proportional: same rate.

concepts.title: External sector and trade
concepts.body:
• Balance of Payments: current account (goods trade, services, remittances, income) plus capital account (FDI, portfolio investment, loans).
  • Rupee devalued in 1966 and 1991. The rupee became fully convertible on the current account in 1994.
  • FEMA (1999) replaced FERA (1973).
  • Devaluation (by government) vs depreciation (by market) of a currency.
  • During colonial rule India exported raw materials and imported finished British goods, with a large export surplus used to pay for the drain.
  • GATT (1947) became the WTO on 1 January 1995 (Geneva). IMF and World Bank came out of Bretton Woods (1944).

concepts.title: Planning and Five-Year Plans
concepts.body:
Planning Commission: 15 March 1950, chaired by the PM. National Development Council: 1952. Replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015 (first Vice-Chairman Arvind Panagariya).

PlanYearsFocus or model
1st1951 to 1956Agriculture; Harrod-Domar model
2nd1956 to 1961Heavy industry; P.C. Mahalanobis model
3rd1961 to 1966Self-reliance; failed due to wars and drought; then plan holiday (1966 to 1969)
4th1969 to 1974Growth with stability
5th1974 to 1979Removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao); ended a year early; rolling plans followed
6th1980 to 1985Poverty removal, employment
7th1985 to 1990Food, work and productivity
8th1992 to 1997Human resource development; after the 1991 reforms
9th1997 to 2002Growth with social justice and equality
10th2002 to 20078% growth target
11th2007 to 2012Faster and more inclusive growth
12th (last)2012 to 2017Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth
  • Pre-independence plans: Bombay Plan (1944, industrialists), Gandhian Plan (1944, S.N. Agarwal), People's Plan (1945, M.N. Roy), Sarvodaya Plan (1950, J.P. Narayan).
  • Industrial Policy Resolutions: 1948 and 1956 (mixed economy). MRTP Act 1969 was replaced by the Competition Act 2002 (CCI).
  • 1991 reforms: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation (LPG); PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh; New Industrial Policy, 24 July 1991.
  • National Investment Fund (2005) holds disinvestment money.

concepts.title: Agriculture
concepts.body:
• Green Revolution (late 1960s): high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation. Norman Borlaug is its world father; M.S. Swaminathan led it in India. Wheat gained the most, then rice; Punjab, Haryana and western UP benefited most. Before it, India had low yields and relied on food imports.
  • White Revolution: milk; Operation Flood (1970); Verghese Kurien (Amul, Anand). India is the largest milk producer.
  • Other revolutions: Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds), Silver (eggs), Golden (horticulture and honey).
  • MSP is announced by the government on the advice of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP, 1965). Food Corporation of India: 1965.
  • Farm schemes: Kisan Credit Card (1998), Soil Health Card (2015), PM Fasal Bima Yojana (2016), e-NAM (2016), PM-KISAN (2019, Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments).

concepts.title: Poverty, employment and indices
concepts.body:
• Poverty line committees: Lakdawala, Tendulkar (2009), Rangarajan (2014). NITI Aayog publishes a Multidimensional Poverty Index.
  • Unemployment types: disguised (more people than needed, common in farming), seasonal, structural, frictional, cyclical. NSO's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) measures it. Agriculture still employs the largest share of India's workers.
  • HDI (UNDP, since 1990; Mahbub ul Haq, with Amartya Sen): health (life expectancy at birth), knowledge (mean years and expected years of schooling), standard of living (GNI per capita, PPP).
  • Gini coefficient and Lorenz curve measure inequality.
  • Neonatal mortality rate: deaths in the first 28 days per 1,000 live births. Infant mortality rate: deaths under 1 year per 1,000 live births. Maternal mortality ratio: per 1,00,000 live births.
  • Programmes: Food for Work (1977), IRDP (1978), TRYSEM (1979), Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989), SGSY (1999), Antyodaya Anna Yojana (2000), MGNREGA (Act 2005, started 2 February 2006, 100 days of work), National Rural Livelihood Mission 'Aajeevika' (2011), National Food Security Act (2013).
  • UN Sustainable Development Goals: 17 goals adopted in 2015 for 2030 (for example Zero Hunger, Quality Education, Climate Action, Life Below Water).

Bharatmala (highways) is under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways; Sagarmala (ports) under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways; UDAN (regional flights) under Civil Aviation.

concepts.title: Markets and financial institutions
concepts.body:
BodyFact
SEBISecurities market regulator; set up 1988, statutory 1992; Mumbai
BSE1875, oldest stock exchange in Asia; index Sensex (30 shares)
NSE1992; index Nifty 50
IRDAIInsurance regulator (1999), Hyderabad
PFRDAPension regulator (2003); runs NPS
LIC1956
IMF, World BankWashington DC
WTOGeneva
Asian Development BankManila
AIIBBeijing
New Development Bank (BRICS)Shanghai

A bull market expects prices to rise; a bear market expects them to fall. An IPO is a company's first sale of shares to the public.

varieties.name: Basic economic concepts
varieties.how: Learn definitions in one line each and the sector of each activity. For market forms, count sellers and buyers.

example.q: A market with only one buyer is called:

varieties.name: National income and inflation
varieties.how: Build national income terms step by step: GDP, add net factor income (GNP), subtract depreciation (NNP), convert to factor cost (national income).

steps: GNP includes the wear and tear of capital.
Removing depreciation gives the net figure, NNP.

varieties.name: Banking, RBI and money
varieties.how: Learn each RBI tool by who holds the money and who pays the rate. Learn nationalisation years and development bank HQs.

example.q: The share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI as cash is called:
steps: SLR is kept by banks themselves in liquid assets.
Cash kept with the RBI is the Cash Reserve Ratio.

varieties.name: Budget, taxes and external sector
varieties.how: Ask: does it create an asset (capital) or not (revenue)? Is the tax burden passed on (indirect) or not (direct)? Learn the three deficit formulas exactly.

example.q: Which of these is an indirect tax: income tax, corporation tax, GST, wealth tax?
steps: Income, corporation and wealth taxes are paid by the person taxed.
GST is collected from the buyer through the seller.

varieties.name: Five-Year Plans and reforms
varieties.how: Learn each plan by number, years and one focus word. The 2nd plan is the Mahalanobis plan; the 12th is the last.

example.q: The Second Five-Year Plan was based on the model of:
steps: The Second Plan (1956 to 1961) stressed heavy industry.
Its model was drawn up by P.C. Mahalanobis.

varieties.name: Agriculture and revolutions
varieties.how: Pair each revolution with its product and leader. Remember the Green Revolution helped wheat most.

steps: It is the White Revolution, led by Verghese Kurien.

varieties.name: Poverty, jobs and development indices
varieties.how: Learn HDI's three dimensions and their indicators, the definitions of IMR and neonatal mortality, and the employment schemes in time order.

example.q: Which indicator measures the 'knowledge' dimension of HDI?
steps: Health uses life expectancy; living standard uses GNI per capita.
Knowledge uses mean and expected years of schooling.
example.answer: Mean and expected years of schooling

varieties.name: Government schemes
varieties.how: Learn scheme, launch year, ministry and target group together. Look for the target group in the scheme name (SVANidhi: street vendors; Ujjwala: LPG).

example.q: PM SVANidhi gives small loans to:
steps: SVANidhi stands for Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi.
It was launched in June 2020 for street vendors.

varieties.name: Markets and financial institutions
varieties.how: Learn regulator and sector pairs (SEBI shares, IRDAI insurance, PFRDA pension) and headquarters of world financial bodies.

example.q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank?
steps: AIIB is in Beijing and NDB in Shanghai.

tips: GDP to national income: G, N, N (GDP, GNP, NNP) then 'at factor cost'.
Repo: RBI lends; reverse repo: RBI borrows. Higher repo means costlier loans and lower inflation.
CRR is Cash with the RBI; SLR is kept by the bank itself (Statutory Liquidity).
Plan focus hook: 1 farms, 2 factories (Mahalanobis), 5 Garibi Hatao, 8 after 1991, 12 last.
Fiscal deficit = borrowing need. Primary deficit = fiscal deficit minus interest.
HDI's three: long life, knowledge, decent living.
traps: WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT), but CPI and IIP are released by NSO (MoSPI).
14 banks were nationalised in 1969 and 6 in 1980; not 20 at once.
The Re 1 note and coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance, not the RBI.
Capital expenditure includes loans given by the government, even though no building is made.
The Planning Commission (1950) was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, not 2014.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
RBI's central office is in Mumbai. It was first in Kolkata (Calcutta) and moved to Mumbai in 1937.
Memory hook: Mumbai = India's money capital = RBI home.

questions.q: GST was introduced in India on:
questions.solution:
GST came into force on 1 July 2017 after the 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016).
Memory hook: 'One nation, one tax' started mid-year: 1-7-17.

questions.q: Which sector includes agriculture and mining?
questions.solution:
The primary sector uses natural resources directly: agriculture, fishing, forestry and mining.
Memory hook: Primary = straight from nature.

questions.q: The portion of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI in the form of cash is called:
questions.solution:
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is kept as cash with RBI. SLR is held by the bank itself in liquid assets such as gold and government securities.
Memory hook: CRR = Cash with the Central bank.

questions.q: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is released by:
options: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
questions.solution:
WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (Ministry of Commerce & Industry). CPI is released by NSO.
Memory hook: Wholesale = trade = Commerce Ministry.

questions.q: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) was based on the model of:
questions.solution:
The Second Plan stressed heavy industry and was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis model. The First Plan used the Harrod–Domar model.
Memory hook: Second plan = 'Steel' = Mahalanobis.

questions.q: How many commercial banks were nationalised in India in July 1969?
questions.solution:
In July 1969, 14 major commercial banks were nationalised. Six more were nationalised in 1980, making 20.
Memory hook: 1969 → 14; 1980 → 6; total 20.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit is best defined as:
options: Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.solution:
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings. It shows how much the government must borrow. Option 3 is revenue deficit; option 4 is primary deficit.
Memory hook: Fiscal deficit = the borrowing need.
